title: Chapter 34
content:
Jakyeong stared at the back of Park Tae-soo’s head as the man drove. Ever since they’d pulled away from Choi Ki-tae’s villa in Gapyeong, not a single word had passed Tae-soo's lips. With Kang Il-hyun’s prior permission in hand, Jakyeong was heading to stay at Il-hyun's luxury penthouse in Seoul tonight. Given the choice between a remote estate surrounded by pitch-black woods and the bustling neon sprawl of the city, Jakyeong vastly preferred the latter.

"Chief Park... Would it be alright if we stopped for coffee on the way? There’s a café I’ve been meaning to check out, and there happens to be a branch right near here..."

Tae-soo met his gaze in the rearview mirror. "Understood. We'll make a stop."

Jakyeong picked up his cloned phone and swiped across the screen, scrolling through Ki-tae’s recent message logs. Half of it was useless chatter, but the rest covered syndicate operations—along with a fair few vulgar remarks about Jakyeong himself.

I want to bend him over. He’s insanely sexy. He’s gorgeous. He's Seok-joo's guest, though—is it safe to touch him?

Jakyeong’s mouth twisted in bitter amusement. Aside from his childhood in the slums, men had rarely dared to be this forward with him. In his line of work, people generally knew that touching the wrong mark meant ending up in a body bag. Yet the moment he stepped foot in Korea, two unhinged bastards had latched onto him like leeches.

The truly ironic part was that both of them were destined to die by his hands anyway.

Shaking off the thought, he pulled up Ki-tae’s calendar. An upcoming event was scheduled just two days from now. It had come up repeatedly in encrypted group chats with his crew.

It appeared to be an offshore gathering hosted aboard a luxury yacht—a high-stakes operation with detailed schedules and protocol memos. Committing the itinerary to memory, he looked up as the sedan smoothly pulled over to the curb. They had arrived outside the boutique café.

With the engine idling, Tae-soo turned around in his seat. "If you tell me your order, I’ll step out and purchase it for you."

"No, please... I need to use the restroom anyway, so I'll run in quickly. What can I get for you, Chief Park?"

"I am fine, thank you."

"My treat. Please let me buy you a cup..."

Feeling awkward turning down the repeated offer, Tae-soo paused, deliberating with an uncharacteristic seriousness that didn't match his intimidating frame.

"In that case... an Ah-Ah."

Jakyeong blinked. "An... Ah-Ah?"

"An Iced Americano."

"Ah... right! The abbreviation... haha..."

Hearing a lethal black-ops veteran casually use trendy Korean slang for iced coffee was almost endearing.

Stepping out of the car, Jakyeong walked inside. This particular franchise had only three locations in the country, and the line here was already snaking toward the entrance. Fiddling with his phone, he glanced through the glass at the dark sedan—the heavy window tint obscured whatever Tae-soo was doing inside.

After waiting his turn, he placed the order and asked the barista for the restroom. Following the clerk's directions toward the rear corridor, he took the receipt and slipped through the back exit.

Inside the men's room, he strode to the very last stall and knocked on the door with a measured, rhythmic cadence:

Tap-tap. Tap-tap-tap. Tap-tap.

The lock turned, the door swung open, and Wang Ryun appeared inside, hauling Jakyeong into the stall by his collar.

"What took you so long? I've been holed up in here for ten minutes."

"Sorry. Did you get the package?"

Ryun reached into his leather jacket, producing a slim kraft-paper envelope. Jakyeong tore it open and inspected the contents. It was an exact replica of the matte-black flash drive sitting in Il-hyun's penthouse safe—even down to the weathered patina, the embossed serial dates, and the precise typography of the English lettering. He planned to swap the drives tonight.

"That specific model was discontinued years ago. Tracking down an authentic casing was a nightmare."

"Thanks, Ryun."

"Still... that guy really gave you free rein over his Seoul penthouse?"

"Yeah."

"Unbelievable. He trusts you enough to hand over the keys to his personal sanctuary?"

Ryun’s face was painted with open bewilderment. Jakyeong couldn't bring himself to confess what had actually transpired between him and Kang Il-hyun. If he did, the Wang brothers would roast him over it until the day he was buried six feet under. Muttering a vague excuse, he pocketed the dummy drive. Lingering any longer would only draw suspicion.

Just then, a sharp knock shook the stall door.

When Jakyeong mirrored the knock in surprise, a low, gravelly voice resonated from the other side.

"Are you in there, Young Master?"

Jakyeong’s blood ran cold.

With practiced agility, Ryun’s massive frame stepped onto the porcelain rim of the toilet, crouching silently against the wall. The two held their breath, keeping their eyes glued to the door panel.

"Just... using the facilities! I'll be right out."

"Is everything alright? I grew concerned, so I came to check."

"Yes, everything is fine. I'll grab the drinks and head out immediately."

"Understood. I will wait by the vehicle."

Jakyeong mouthed a silent, breathless curse.

Heavy footsteps echoed across the tile until the outer door clicked shut. Ryun raised an eyebrow, silently asking who that was, but Jakyeong shook his head, pressing an index finger to his lips. He peered through the gap beneath the stall—empty.

Flashing Ryun a hand signal to clear out, Jakyeong slipped out of the stall and returned to the café counter.

Just as he reached the register, the wireless pager buzzed in his palm. Collecting the two iced coffees in a cardboard carrier, he walked back to the sedan. Tae-soo was seated behind the wheel, staring impassively through the windshield.

Jakyeong retrieved one of the cups and offered it forward. "Here you go. It's nice and cold."

"Thank you."

Tae-soo pulled hard on the straw, draining half the cup in a few deep draughts before shifting the car into gear. Their eyes met briefly in the rearview mirror several times during the drive, but Tae-soo offered no further questions.

[You secured the full client ledger, right?]

[Yes, Father. I compiled a dedicated roster for the VIPs and transmitted the encrypted file to your terminal. Please verify it. Our teams at the boarding gate will handle guest invitations and conduct rigorous physical pat-downs. You don't need to worry.]

[I am placing my complete trust in you, Ki-tae. With Jun-tae gone, you must carry his weight as well.]

[I understand, Father. Trust me—I won't allow a single mistake.]

Soaking in the steaming bathwater, Jakyeong leaned his head back against the porcelain rim. The master tub in Il-hyun's penthouse was cavernous, leaving ample room even for his long limbs. Dragging on his e-cigarette, he let his arm dangle over the edge, plumes of gray vapor blending with the rising steam.

The live audio intercept from the Choi family’s wiretap played through the speaker. In two days, the father and son were hosting a private gala aboard a chartered yacht. A "charity gala" in name only—in reality, it was a massive, high-end narcotics distribution ring catering to high-society VIPs, political heavyweights, and entertainment moguls.

After several more minutes of operational back-and-forth, the call terminated.

Jakyeong crushed out his smoke, tossed the butt, and flushed it away. Stepping up to the vanity mirror, his eyes landed on the angry, coin-sized crimson mark branded into the side of his neck. He scowled, rubbing the bruised skin with his thumb, but the hickey remained as vivid as ever.

Clicking his tongue in irritation, he finished his shower and slipped into a plush bathrobe.

Walking into the expansive living room, he cracked open a cold beer, propping his feet up on the glass table. Resting beside his glass was the counterfeit drive Ryun had delivered. What kind of catastrophic blackmail is stored on the original to command a bounty equal to an assassination contract? Curiosity clawed at him, but viewing the contents was a strict breach of professional protocol.

He downed the beer in long, steady gulps. The cold liquid chased away the dry burn in his throat, a subtle buzz settling over his nerves. Deciding against a second can, he scooped up the dummy drive and stood.

He performed a methodical electronic sweep across the parlor and bedrooms, ensuring zero listening bugs or hidden lenses were active.

Park Tae-soo was currently stationed in the adjacent penthouse unit next door, entirely blind to what was happening within these walls.

Slipping on a pair of ultra-thin tactical gloves to avoid leaving latent prints, Jakyeong strode toward the primary study. He pushed the sliding bookshelf aside, pressed the concealed wall panel, and stepped into the hidden auxiliary office.

Kneeling beneath the executive desk, the heavy digital safe sat right where he’d left it.

He punched in the eight-digit passcode from memory. The internal locking bolts disengaged with a clean mechanical hum.

Gently pulling the heavy steel door open, the rows of labeled flash drives gleamed under his penlight. The target drive was resting in its designated slot.

Jakyeong lifted the authentic drive, slipped it into his robe pocket, and slotted Ryun’s counterfeit unit into the empty bracket.

He swung the safe door shut, a triumphant smile tugging at his lips.

One objective down.

Now that the collateral was in hand, moving into Chairman Kang’s main estate sounded increasingly practical. The old patriarch had explicitly invited him to stay, after all. He’d test the waters with Kang Seok-joo tomorrow.

Remaining under Kang Il-hyun’s thumb until the inauguration felt like a fast track to dying of sheer psychological stress.

As he turned to leave, his eyes caught a thick, leather-bound volume resting on the lowest shelf. Among the sea of economic texts and ledgers, it was the only photo album.

Curiosity getting the better of him, Jakyeong pulled the album down and flipped to the first page.

A photograph of an infant greeted him. Kang Il-hyun? Standing beside the bassinet was a slightly older girl wrapping her arms around the baby with a bright, luminous smile—a young Kang Yu-jung.

He turned the page. The boy in the pictures had grown into a toddler, yet his face was completely hollowed of emotion. In photo after photo, Yu-jung beamed brightly at the lens while young Il-hyun simply stared into the camera with dead, unblinking eyes.

Even as a small child, he had an unsettlingly cold aura.

Flipping through the subsequent years, not a single snapshot captured the boy smiling. Jakyeong found his mind drifting back to his own fractured childhood. He, too, had worn that exact same hollow mask every day of his youth. Had photographs of young Jakyeong survived, they would have looked virtually identical to Il-hyun's.

Past middle school, family photos ceased entirely. Aside from a few standard identification portraits, the rest of the album was sparse.

A high school portrait of Il-hyun in a uniform showed a teenager radiating raw, dangerous defiance—a sharp jaw set in stubborn pride, eyes smoldering with untamed hostility.

Jakyeong smiled faintly, turning the page. The remaining sleeves were completely blank.

He had hoped to catch a glimpse of Il-hyun’s late mother, but not a single picture of her existed. Strangely enough, there wasn't a single photograph of his living father either. Even his elementary school graduation photo featured only Il-hyun and his sister standing alone before the gates.

Jakyeong closed the album and returned it precisely to its slot.

Stepping back into the living room, he fetched a fresh beer from the fridge, settled onto the sofa, and switched on the integrated sound system. A rich, sweeping classical orchestration filled the cavernous penthouse.

Can in hand, Jakyeong walked over to the floor-to-ceiling glass, taking in the panoramic vista of nighttime Seoul.

Sprawling highways and city lights wove through the dark metropolis like glittering rivers of gold. Flowing through the stereo speakers was the iconic Queen of the Night aria from Mozart's The Magic Flute.

Jakyeong took a slow sip of beer, a wry, bitter smile touching his lips.

A remarkably fitting soundtrack.

Had Kang Il-hyun stood before this very window, listening to this exact aria while looking down over the city? What had occupied his thoughts? Like the Queen of the Night herself... had he spent his nights drowning in hatred, cursing the bloodline that brought him into this world?

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Ah-Ah (아아): Ubiquitous Korean slang/abbreviation for Iced Americano (아이스 아메리카노). In South Korea, iced coffee is a cultural staple consumed year-round (spawning the popular slang Eol-juk-ah, meaning "even if I freeze to death, iced Americano"). Tae-soo casually using this slang humanizes his otherwise stoic, frightening presence.

  • Queen of the Night Aria (밤의 여왕 아리아): Mozart's famous aria (Der Hölle Rache kocht in meinem Herzen) from The Magic Flute, sung by the Queen of the Night as she places a dagger in her daughter's hand and commands her to assassinate her rival. The themes of vengeful parental manipulation, matricide, and lethal family betrayal heavily parallel the dark dynastic war within Haewon Group.
